gates.description: Every model must have a clearly defined grain (one row represents what?) in its documentation
Primary key must be tested for uniqueness and not-null on every model
Every model and column must have a description — undocumented columns should not exist
Business metric definitions must be agreed with stakeholders before SQL implementation
All schema and data tests must pass in CI — failed tests block merge
Naming conventions must be followed (stg_, int_, fct_, dim_ prefixes; _at, _id, is_ suffixes)

anti_patterns.description: Five different tables calculate revenue five different ways — every dashboard shows a different number
Analysts write long SQL directly against raw data — no version control, no tests, no shared logic
Models deployed without tests — a source change silently produces wrong numbers for weeks
Hundreds of models, none documented — new analysts can't understand what stg_evt_usr_int_v2 means
All transformations in a single 500-line SQL model — impossible to test, debug, or reuse

escalation_triggers: Two teams using different definitions for the same metric and cannot agree
Source data quality issues that transformations cannot fix — data engineering intervention needed
Stakeholder requesting a metric that cannot be reliably calculated from available data
Performance issues: critical dbt models taking too long to build
Breaking change in source data affecting many downstream models and dashboards
Compliance requirement for data retention or deletion affecting model design

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with data modeling requirements and metric definitions

output_certifications: Every model has a clearly defined grain in its documentation
Primary key tested for uniqueness and not-null on every model
All models and columns have descriptions in schema.yml
Business metric definitions agreed with stakeholders before SQL implementation
All schema and data tests pass in CI
Naming conventions followed (stg_, int_, fct_, dim_ prefixes)
